title: BorderBeam
description: Decorative component that renders a moving beam along a container border.
whenToUse:
- Use when a container needs stronger visual emphasis without introducing business state semantics.
- Suitable for login panels, recommendation cards, AI modules, and key CTA blocks.
- As a decorative effect, it should not replace focus rings, validation borders, or status feedback.

examples.name: Basic
examples.description: Basic usage. Wrap any container with `BorderBeam` to add a continuous decorative beam effect along its border.

examples.name: Show on hover
examples.description: Hide the border beam by default, and reveal it when hovering over the container.

examples.name: Multiple beams
examples.description: Use `count` to set the number of beams. Multiple beams are evenly distributed around the container border. It should be a positive integer, and the default value is `1`.

examples.name: Custom container
examples.description: A custom container can also host `BorderBeam`. The beam layer is inserted into the child node and positioned with `position: absolute` along the container edge, so the host element needs to provide a positioning context. In most cases, set `position: relative`.

examples.name: Gradients
examples.description: Display six gradient beam palettes and switch between them.

examples.name: Duration
examples.description: Use `duration` to control how many seconds the beam takes to complete one loop. The default is 6 seconds.

examples.name: Size
examples.description: Use `size` to control the size of the visible beam segment. The default is `100px`, and numbers are treated as pixels.

examples.name: Line width
examples.description: Use `lineWidth` to adjust the beam width of an individual BorderBeam. The default value is `1px`, and numbers are treated as pixels.

rows: Beam color configuration. Supports a single color string or gradient stops. `percent` uses the `0 ~ 100` input range and BorderBeam reserves tail space for the transparent fade
Time in seconds for the beam to complete one loop
Width of the beam line. Numbers are treated as pixels
Outset distance of the beam layer from the container edge. Set to `0` for clipped containers
Size of the visible beam segment. Numbers are treated as pixels
